messages:
sara: heads up, starting edge shadow swap -> green in ap-southeast, will flip weights gradually. keeping TTL low (60s). watching dashboards.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT OPENED: spike in 5xx and error rate in ap-southeast edge cluster. Severity: P1. Paging oncall. runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/edge-rollout|edge-rollout runbook>
mike: seeing 502/504s from the logging tail around 15:42 UTC, spike aligns with weight flip to green ~15:40. Not consistent across POPs.
jen: can you paste the deploy id? I want to check pods and LB health.
sara: deploy id `deploy/edge-green-20250315-72b` - started canary at 15:39, moved 30% at 15:40, 60% at 15:41.
mike: quick network check — some clients still resolving to the old blue IPs. suspect DNS TTL behavior + CNAME alias split. run: `dig +short @8.8.8.8 edge.ap-southeast.redwood.example` returns two IPs, one in blue pool and one in green.
jen: run `kubectl get pods -n edge -l release=edge-green` => some readiness probes flapping. logs show `upstream connect error or disconnect` in proxy.
net-ops: we didn't change any global DNS config but noticed the edge CNAME was split across two edge-proxies during the swap. TTL on the CNAME was 300s for some records due to cached responses from our vendor.
matt: paging in — I'm oncall. Can you confirm customer impact?
ali: CS: a handful of enterprise customers in AP reported 5xx in product, ~6 customers opened chats, affected workflows are inference calls and document ingestion. severity customer-facing.
deploy-bot: rollback command available: `/deploy rollback deploy/edge-green-20250315-72b --region ap-southeast` (requires approval).
sara: option A: pause rollout and hold weights. Option B: kill feature-flag to route all to blue. Option C: full rollback. Thoughts?
mike: kill the flag quickly. flag flip is fastest, DNS caches will continue to trickle but we'll remove the split backend immediately.
jen: agree. issuing kill-switch now. `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" https://flags.internal/edge/green/enable -d '{"state": "off"}'`
jen: (response) 200 OK — flag flipped. traffic should stop routing to green at the routing layer.
incident-bot: action logged: feature flag `edge.green.enabled` set to `false` by jen at 15:46 UTC.
mike: checking metrics — errors dropping in ap-southeast within one minute, but still some client errors (likely cached DNS).
net-ops: started an emergency TTL purge request with DNS vendor, asked for cache flushes and lowered authoritative TTL to 30s. ETA ~2-5 minutes.
matt: good. CS: Ali please send templated notice to affected customers with current mitigation and ETA.
ali: sending now. message: "We've temporarily routed traffic away from the new edge pool and are monitoring. Expected full recovery within 5-10 minutes as caches clear. Apologies for the disruption."
jen: to be safe I'm starting a controlled rollback of the green replicas: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/edge-green -n edge` and scaling down green to 0/10.
deploy-bot: rollback started for deploy/edge-green-20250315-72b by jen. watch: `kubectl rollout status deployment/edge-green -n edge`
mike: proxy logs look stable, 5xxs near baseline now. Cloudfront errors trending down.
incident-bot: updated status: mitigation in place (feature-flag kill + DNS purge); monitoring recovery.
sara: postmortem todo: TTL validation in preflight, vendor cache invalidation checklist, make flag kill path one-click from deploy UI. Also add a gating step to prevent CNAME split during weight flips.
matt: handing off to morning oncall for follow-up and postmortem. I'll leave incident open until metrics are stable for 30m.
jen: leaving logs and timing notes in the incident channel, stack traces attached to the ticket.
ali: CS follow-up scheduled in 30m to confirm any lingering customerism.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: error rates back to baseline as of 15:57 UTC. Resolution: feature flag kill + DNS vendor purge + rollback of green replicas. Severity downgraded.
sara: thanks team. postmortem owner: jen. I'll add action items to the tracker. :white_check_mark:
